changedFields.after: The extent to which observed changes can be attributed to the intervention rather than other factors.

changedFields.before: Internal validity refers to whether the observed changes in an experiment are truly caused by the intervention being tested, meaning the experiment accurately measures the intended cause-and-effect relationship. Generalizability relates to external validity, consistency to reliability, and replication to reproducibility.
changedFields.after: Internal validity concerns causal attribution: whether the intervention rather than other factors explains the observed change. Measuring the intended construct is a different measurement-quality question; consistency is reliability, and generalizing to other populations is external validity. The correct option remains1.
